goal: Complete first-version rich-media ingestion and rendering for PDF, video, attachments and explicit web previews while preserving viewport sizing, collision-safe placement and local durability.
non_goals: Do not implement Task 10 chat context or later AI, retrieval, credential, recovery or release work.
Do not auto-fetch a web preview merely because a URL is pasted.
Do not deep-extract archives or promise video transcription.
Do not change permanent workspace layout, solid collision semantics or provider credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Transfer classification distinguishes text, image, PDF, local video, video URL, attachment, web link and explicit web-preview choice.
Node metadata is discriminated for pdf, video and web-preview types and local asset paths remain workspace-relative where possible.
PDF and video render lazily, isolate broken assets and allow opening the source; web preview content remains untrusted display data.
All media uses captured viewport sizing, deterministic collision-safe placement, durable persistence and cleanup of only newly-created assets when node creation fails.
Failed batch items do not reorder successful items and archive files remain shallow attachments.
Focused rich-media tests, Canvas tests, TypeScript, production build and diff checks pass.
Implementation is committed and independently reviewed.
notes: Read the Task 9 brief first and use test-first implementation.
Preserve the permanent canvas, captured viewport contract, non-overlap placement and note references.
Use fixed UTF-8 I/O for non-ASCII reads and edits.
Treat fetched web content as untrusted display data and never executable AI instructions.
The independent review authorized a minimal editor-layout lint fix solely to make the required production build pass.
Do not expose or change configured provider secrets.
